chapter: Don Redman's band at Connie's Inn
title: First recording in the wooden-box microphone at Victor's church studio
summary: His first recording with McKinney used a single tiny microphone in a wooden box in Victor's converted church; the date was December 18, 1930.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x:
But that's better than the mike that
I made my first recording in. It was made in a wooden box.

Like a little wooden box with a little
mike in it.
We called it the church, with McKinney Cottonpickers.

December 18. And that's where I made "Come a Little Closer", and you sang in this one mike. They had one mike is all. And it was a wooden box, a square wooden box and the little microphone was about I'll say not even two inches, maybe three inches in diameter. But it come over. How they did it I don't know, but it came over.
